newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Traders divided over price movement in Budapest mk.
newsitem.headline: Traders divided over price movement in Budapest mk.

text.p: Hungarian traders were divided as to which direction shares will move on Tuesday with some believing prices will rise on weak supply and others seeing falling prices due to the expiry of June futures.
Some expected prices to move upwards on the back of generally positive market sentiment in Hungary and on major foreign markets and of weak supply of Hungarian shares.
"Cheap shares have disappeared from the market...and buyers can acquire bigger amounts of stocks only at higher prices," said Tamas Petheo of Buda-Cash Brokerhaz.
But others said prices would decline as June BUX futures expire and this might trigger selling pressure on the spot market.

"There are houses with hedge deals and the share arm of these deals have to be closed on Tuesday. This will go with fairly strong selling pressure," said Peter Lencs of MKB Securities, adding he still believed the overall trend was upward.
In its weekly market report Raiffeisen Securities also anticipated an increasing trend in prices continuing this week.
"The improving macroeconomic background and the favourable performance of blue chip companies encourage the current price increase from the fundamental side," Raiffeisen said.
On Monday the BUX index finished at 6,327.12 points, up 36.77.
